Two invariants from the R0.4.3 review:

R0.4.4 linearity & non-leakage model — written before the mechanism

Two invariants from the R0.4.3 review:

A descendant capability must never reveal material sufficient to reconstruct an ancestor capability.

Evidence may be Copy. Authority-bearing transition tokens may not be Copy, Clone, repeatably derivable, or reproducible from immutable inputs. A value being non-copyable is not enough; authority must have a non-forking derivation.

Non-leakage

Every provenance-bearing type carried the root mark and derived Debug; derived Debug prints private fields, so any holder of an honest event could recover the world-global mark and, bootstrap being public, reconstruct root authority — descendant→ancestor amplification. Closure:

  • Manual Debug for every mark-bearing type; the mark renders as

<redacted>. No Display/Hash/serialization impls exist.

  • PartialEq/Eq removed from all mark-bearing types: equality over a

secret is a guess-oracle, and nothing in replay needs record equality.

  • A DOWNSTREAM test (cd-node, not in-crate) formats every public

diagnostic surface with a distinctive mark and proves the bytes are absent.

  • Documented authority-amplification boundary: the same raw bytes that

tag descendants are what bootstrap accepts. Without cryptographic one-way derivation (out of scope for no_std R0, and faking one with an invertible permutation would be worse than honesty), redaction plus the absence of any read-back API is the containment. A deployment must replace marks with derived/attested material; stated on the skepticism list.

Claim narrowed (per review)

Not "unforgeable within a process" — type privacy is not hostile-process isolation. The enforceable claim: safe-Rust API-level unforgeability for callers that do not possess ancestor capabilities or bootstrap material. cd-core itself remains #![forbid(unsafe_code)].

Linear custody (the transition diagram, every arrow linear)

LocusRoot ──begin()──────────────► Vacant(L,0) + FinalityWarden + Admission(0)
Vacant(L,N) + Admission ──attach(c)──► Attached(L,c,N) + AttachRecord(N) + Admission'  [no recovery value exists]
Attached ──detach()──────────────► Vacant(L,N+1) + DetachReceipt(N)
Attached ──suspend()─────────────► CarrierCustody(N)                       [CONSUMES live: Live XOR Recoverable]
CarrierCustody(N) + &Admission ──recover──► Attached(L,c,N)              [CONSUMES custody; judged vs CURRENT admission]
Warden + Admission ──finalize_loss► LossFinalization + Vacant(L,N+1) + Admission'   [atomic; R0.4.7]
(every transition above also consumes and returns the Admission — docs/admission-model.md)

  • R0.4.5 invariant: **a recovery representation of possession must be

mutually exclusive with live possession, unless an external fencing primitive proves only one can become active.** The R0.4.4 shape (custody minted at attach beside the live value) violated this by aliasing; the former custody() accessor is gone for the same reason. Now custody exists only by consuming the live attachment, and recovery consumes the custody. Two operational attachments for one locus/carrier/generation cannot be derived via any safe-Rust API.

  • Reopen was removed in R0.4.7: finality now materializes the successor

vacancy atomically with the admission advance, so an accepted closure yields exactly one vacancy within one lineage by construction. A trusted root can still mint parallel lineages via repeated create_locus; global Locus-birth uniqueness is a future World-level invariant.

  • The root's create_locus(same id) repeatability remains an explicitly

trusted-root act, stated, outside the linearity claim.

What linearity does and does not give (persistence honesty)

The R0 property is linear checkpointed restart/reconstitution in safe Rust: a planned suspend() then recover. An unplanned crash cannot call a consuming transition first, so unplanned crash recovery is NOT modeled or claimed. Durable persistence inherently copies bytes (RAM/disk/backup/journal), so !Clone is not evidence of durable single-use semantics. Durable recovery will need an explicitly modeled primitive (incarnation counters over monotonic/CAS storage, secure-element monotonicity, or supervisor fencing) — deliberately NOT designed in R0.4.4; claimed nowhere.

Consequently the possession claim in STATUS is corrected to: single-log replay accepts at most one Carrier per generation, with capability-graph forking limits (trusted-root duplicate genesis; durable copies of custody bytes) stated explicitly.

Falsifiers this model must survive

  1. Debug of every public diagnostic surface contains no mark bytes

(downstream test).

  1. attachment.custody() no longer exists (compile gate).

  2. A consumed custody cannot be used twice (compile gate); recovery

yields exactly one successor.

  1. A consumed admission cannot be reused (compile gate); one accepted

closure yields exactly one successor vacancy (finality is atomic).

  1. All R0.4.1–R0.4.3 falsifiers still pass unchanged in meaning.
